subject: Alternatives or Workarounds for googleVis Dynamic Map

messages.author: 58f3bf7dd079cc0d
messages.subject: Alternatives or Workarounds for googleVis Dynamic Map
parts:
Hey all,

I have been using googleVis to make interactive, dynamic maps as described by Ryan Peek here. The described method makes a very nice, clean map with markers that will display additional information about a point when clicked on. Since this outputs as html/javascript, it would be great to host on our project website. Unfortunately, Google Charts API (which the googleVis package utilizes) only allows for a map of 400 markers at a time (as described in the documentation here. Some of the datasets I would like to map have over 3000 records! Does anyone know of a similar alternative for making a dynamic, web-hostable map, or possibly a way to trick Google Charts into displaying more records? I don't have much hope for the latter solution, but I figured this was the place to ask.

Cheers,
Nate Hamlet

messages.author: 8c8f0ca54c4a2459
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Alternatives or Workarounds for googleVis Dynamic Map
parts:
Hi nate,

The leaflet package (whose predecessor, leafletR, was presented by Michele in that same video), doesn't have any limits to markers as far as I know, and is very good for making web-embeddable, dynamic maps: https://rstudio.github.io/leaflet/

You will likely want to use clustering so that thousands of markers don't appear at once - this is a big computational load for any browser.  Clustering groups nearby markers together until the zoom is high enough to distinguish them.  This keeps too many points from ever having to be rendered at once.  Details at https://rstudio.github.io/leaflet/markers.html#marker-clusters
